rationale.text: No link and candidate none. The test applies to each <canvas> element that is a text image carrying information. Whether an image displays text is a matter of what its pixels show, which code reading the page cannot establish; whether it carries information is judgment. The two routes are judgment as well: whether a graphic effect can be reproduced in CSS, and whether a mechanism really replaces the images with styled text. So are the five particular cases: a logo, a brand name, a CAPTCHA, an image-test, or an image whose exact rendering is essential. No check could fault an image without knowing that it shows text and that no exception applies. No axe-core rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment, because whether any text image is present is not known from the code. Needs is state: confirming a replacement mechanism means activating it and seeing the images replaced. A canvas is drawn by script, so even its drawing calls do not show reliably whether text was drawn.
